Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Smt. Kamla Singh, learned counsel for applicant and Shri Vibhav Anand Singh, learned
A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Crime No.606 of 2019, under
Sections 498A, 304B, 342 Ipc & 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Police Station Kasia, District
Kushinagar with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

4.  As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Muslim Rights on 18.01.2019 and the applicant is stated to have subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry of a motorcycle and Rs.50,000/- leading to her death on 12.10.2019.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Admittedly, this was the third marriage of the applicant and his earlier two wives had expired and it was the first marriage of the deceased person.

Learned counsel has further stated that the informant and the mother of the deceased were present at the time of inquest proceedings which was undertaken after lodging of the FIR on 13.10.2019 at 12:22 pm.

Learned counsel has further stated that there are material contradictions in the statement of PW-1 and PW-2 with respect to recording of the inquest proceedings whereby they have categorically stated that the dead body of the decease was sent to mortuary in the morning on 13.10.2019 itself.
Learned counsel has further stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence and was 55 years of age at the time of marriage has three children to take care of.
The said three siblings have been forced to lead a life of destitution and vagrancy owing to the applicant being incarcerated.
Learned counsel has further stated that the cause of death has been assigned as strangulation and no role has been assigned to the applicant.
All the witnesses of fact have been examined and there is no likelihood of the applicant tampering with evidence whatsoever.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 15.10.2019.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the deceased had expired within a period of nine months of her marriage who was a young lady of 25 years.

Learned A.G.A. has further stated that in all nine injuries on the body of the deceased person have been observed by the doctor conducting the autopsy and it has been opined that the deceased had expired due to asphyxia as a result of strangulation.

Learned A.G.A. has further stated that the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant and the onus lies on the applicant to explain the reasons of her death, although he could not dispute the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents to his credit.
Learned A.G.A. has further stated that the trial is at its conclusive end as already five witnesses have been examined.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the evidence on record, and also taking into consideration the fact that the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant that too within a period of nine months of her marriage, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order or as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
